sentences.text: Oral Order
(PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)

1. By means of the present petition, the petitioners seek to challenge the order dated 31.1.2024 passed by the Collector, Surat in Reference (Delay) Case No. 6 of 2023, whereby the application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Settlement Act, 2013 filed by the petitioners for making of Reference seeking re-determination of compensation pursuant to award dated 22.9.2020, which was revised/ rectified by order dated 20.3.2021 passed by the competent authority.

sentences.text: The contentions in the writ petition is that the petitioners were not served with the copy of the award and there is no prohibition of limitation insofar as the objections NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/187/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined are concerned, are as vague as they could be.
3. It is contended by the petitioners that an order for valuation of trees standing over the land in question which have been acquired had been passed on 22.5.2023.
The reference application under Section 64 was filed on 26.5.2023.

In the order impugned, the Collector records that even if benefit of condonation of limitation as given by the Apex Court in case of Suo-Motu Writ Petition (Civil)
No.(s) 3 of 2020 during the Covid-19 period was given to the petitioners, the reference was beyond 1 year and 6 months, which is more than a maximum time period provided under the first and second proviso of subsection (2) of Section 64, within which Collector can entertain application for making reference under Section 64.
4.

It is opined that the Collector has no jurisdiction to condone the delay beyond the time period provided in the subsection (2) of Section 64 as the powers of the Collector to condone the delay are circumspect by the time period provided under statutory provision itself.

5. Assailing this order, it is submitted by learned advocate for the petitioners that since the award for valuation of trees over the land in question was passed on 25.3.2023 much after the making of the application under Section 64, it cannot be said that the petitioners have committed any delay and moreover similar applications filed by other tenure holders, the owners of the same survey number, adjacent parcels of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/187/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined land have been entertained by the Collector by condoning the delay and making of the reference to the competent authority.

Both these submissions do not detain us for long, for the simple reason that in view of the categorical provision, the time period provided in 1st and 2nd proviso to the said sub- section, the Collector did not have jurisdiction to condone the jurisdiction beyond the period of 1 years 6 weeks, in the case of the petitioner.

Being liberal, the Collector had even condone the time period taken during the onset of Covid-19, i.e. 20.2.2021 till 20.2.2022, in view of the order of the Apex Court though the petitioners had filed the application under Section 64 after a period of 1 year and 3 months of the expiry of extended period of limitation under the order of Apex Court, which was 20.2.2022.
6.
There is no dispute about the computations made by the Collector.
The only issue raised by the petitioners is that the other similarly situated persons have been given benefit of limitation.
This submission also has been made at the bar and no foundation has been laid in the writ petition itself.

On asking of the Court, learned advocate for the petitioners would submit that it has come to his knowledge only in the morning that application of the similarly situated persons application has been allowed by the Collector and reference has been entertained.
7. This submission being made at the bar cannot be entertained.

However, in case other persons similarly situated had been able to file their reference and their reference are NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/187/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined pending before the competent authority,
the petitioners would still have a remedy in the shape of Section 73 which provides for Jayaben Manilal Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12985970/
2 re-determination of the amount of compensation on the basis of award passed by the competent authority.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the eventuality, the reference application of those land holders who are similarly situated as that of the petitioners herein are allowed, a remedy would be available to the petitioners under Section 73.
8.
For the aforesaid, no interference is called for.
The petition stands dismissed.

However, it is provided that in the event, the petitioners avail remedy under Section 73 at the relevant point of time, the dismissal of the reference application on the ground of delay and the present petition by this order shall not come in the way of the petitioners.
Direct Service is permitted.
